1. Abstract

Urban Heat Islands (UHIs) represent one of the deadliest and most accelerating consequences of global climate change, disproportionately threatening densifying global South metropolises. While modern satellite Earth Observation (EO) produces petabytes of thermal surface data, municipal authorities encounter an insurmountable operational chasm between detection and capital allocation. Urban planners lack mathematically grounded spatial optimization models, municipal finance officers face unquantified capital risk without auditable cost-benefit trade-offs, and civic interventions suffer from zero empirical post-deployment verification.

CLIMORA is an open, deterministic, enterprise-grade Decision Layer and Climate Action Operating System designed to convert satellite microclimate analytics into fundable, mathematically optimized, and cryptographically governed urban intervention projects. Validated across the statutory boundary of Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC)—spanning 312.11 km² and 5,011,229 residents—CLIMORA discretizes the urban surface into 3,181 Uber H3 Resolution-9 hexagons (~0.0986 km² each). Integrating a 5-year pre-monsoon peak-summer thermal composite (Landsat 8/9 Collection 2 Level-2, 2021–2025), high-resolution Sentinel-2 multispectral vegetation/built-up indices, and WorldPop dasymetric population counts, CLIMORA operationalizes the IPCC AR6 Hazard–Exposure–Vulnerability (HEV) risk framework under an unyielding Zero-Exposure Axiom.

To resolve capital scarcity, CLIMORA couples spatial econometrics (Local Moran's I) with a HiGHS Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) optimization engine. Under a canonical ₹1 Crore (₹10,000,000) municipal budget preset, CLIMORA isolates the top 28 priority hex cells (just 0.88% of the city's landmass), allocating 2,695 shade trees to shelter 118,941 vulnerable citizens (mean 4,248 residents/cell vs. citywide mean 1,575) at an average modeled cooling reduction of ~0.07 °C to 0.17 °C. CLIMORA completes the project lifecycle by implementing Amazon Cedar attribute-based access control (ABAC) with seven ratified governance policies, guaranteeing complete immutability of scientific truth layers while enforcing strict statutory separation between planners, municipal treasurers, field contractors, and ISO 14064-2 accredited MRV auditors.

Governing Axiom — Evidence Truth Badges: Every metric in CLIMORA carries a classified truth badge: OBSERVED Satellite sensor radiances • DERIVED Deterministic mathematical synthesis • MODELED HiGHS optimization outputs • BUILT Production codebase • PLANNED Empirical field MRV protocol.

2. Problem Statement

Rapid urbanization across Indian metropolises has replaced vegetative canopy with dense, heat-absorbing concrete and asphalt. In Pune, peak-summer surface temperatures regularly exceed 45.0 °C. However, public mitigation remains paralyzed by three fundamental institutional failures:

1. Spatial Disconnect

Satellites observe continuous pixels; municipal commissioners manage political wards. Coarse administrative boundaries obscure micro-heat pockets.

2. Capital Allocation Vacuum

Climate capital is finite. Municipalities lack mathematical optimization tools to determine where each rupee yields maximum citizen protection.

3. Zero Empirical Verification

Civic greening initiatives operate with zero post-deployment auditing. Without counterfactual baseline audits, cooling claims remain unverified.

4. Core Objectives

  • Equi-Area Discretization: Partition PMC's 312.11 km² statutory territory into 3,181 uniform Uber H3 Res-9 hexagons (~0.0986 km² each) to guarantee spatial invariance.
  • Thermal Baseline Freezing: Build an empirical 5-year pre-monsoon baseline (April 2021–2025) using cloud-free USGS Landsat 8/9 thermal radiance.
  • Zero-Exposure Risk Modeling: Codify the IPCC AR6 framework ensuring uninhabited hot spots yield zero human risk.
  • Mathematical Capital Allocation: Solve a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) optimization model under 5 budget presets within a 5% optimality gap.
  • Cryptographic Governance: Implement Amazon Cedar ABAC with 7 ratified policies and strict negative anti-tampering guards.

6. Technology Stack

Analytical & Backend Infrastructure

  • Language: Python 3.11+, Rust FFI (via cedarpy)
  • Solver Engine: HiGHS (scipy.optimize.milp) branch-and-cut
  • Geospatial Processing: Rasterio, GeoPandas, PyArrow, Libpysal
  • API Service Boundary: Flask 2.3.2, Gunicorn, Pydantic schemas
  • Security & Authorization: Amazon Cedar Policy Engine
  • Storage & Data Lake: Apache Parquet (Snappy), Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF

Presentation & Cloud Deployment

  • Frontend Framework: React 18, Vite, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS
  • Mapping Engine: MapLibre GL, Leaflet, H3-JS vector renderer
  • Icons & Design: Lucide Icons, Headless UI, Custom Dark Navy Palette
  • Cloud Infrastructure: AWS S3 (Data Lake), ECS Fargate, AWS Amplify
  • Verification Test Suite: Pytest (188 backend tests), Vitest (25 UI tests)

Analytical Findings on Spatial Stability & Efficiency

The empirical results confirm three critical operational properties of the CLIMORA optimization engine:

  • Monotonic Investment Inclusion: As municipal capital increases from ₹5 Lakh to ₹1 Crore, previously selected cells remain funded, preventing fragmented multi-year municipal planning.
  • Extreme Population Concentration: Under the ₹1 Crore portfolio, CLIMORA concentrates capital on just 0.88% of PMC's landmass (2.76 km²) while directly sheltering 118,941 residents (averaging 4,248 residents/cell vs. citywide mean 1,575), achieving a 2.7× density super-concentration factor.
  • Thermodynamic Safety Boundaries: All allocated interventions remain well within the 4.0 °C intra-cell cooling saturation cap, guaranteeing realistic biophysical performance without mathematical artifacts.
